currentUserGoal: Raise the visual resolution of the giant one-tile field so its close-up presentation no longer magnifies a 58x58 texture into visibly oversized blocks.
workCompleted: Measured the existing field atlas and confirmed every normal tile texture is only 58x58 pixels while the authored one-tile plot displays at up to 420x420.
Added eight deterministic 256x256 procedural pixel-art surfaces, one for every ecosystem TileStage from Dormant through Rooted.
Authored stage-specific high-detail soil, stubble, grass tufts, clover, dew, wet patches, wildflowers, pollen, roots, moss, and mushrooms instead of applying a blurred upscale.
Added layered ground cover and irregular multi-blade tufts so the higher-resolution meadow remains dense and organic rather than sparse or uniformly patterned.
Switched only the single-plot near view to the new hero texture tier; expanded fields retain the compact 58x58 variants, tile pooling, chunk summaries, and existing LOD behavior.
Kept the generated surfaces cached for the life of the ecosystem scene, with no per-frame canvas work and no texture creation proportional to logical tile count.
Added contract tests covering all eight unique texture keys, the 256px hero size, deterministic unique seeds, positive detail density, and valid stage palettes.
verificationRun: npm run check passed: ESLint, 108 Vitest tests across 15 files, TypeScript, and the Vite production build.
Browser visual verification passed for the one-tile field at 1280x720 desktop and 390x844 phone viewports.
The Wildflower Patch was observed live with individually readable pink, yellow, white, and blue flowers instead of the former magnified 58px blocks.

The redesign-specific 32x32 check reported 1,024 logical tiles, mid LOD, 16 rendered chunk views, zero full-field scans, zero frame spikes, and a 23.62ms recorded maximum frame delta during the sample.
No browser errors or warnings were reported.
